Machine Learning.description: A subfield of artificial intelligence that enables computers to learn from data
Machine Learning.reference: Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence that focuses on building systems that learn from and make decisions based on data. Instead of being explicitly programmed to perform a task, machine learning models are trained on large datasets to identify patterns and make predictions. Key types include supervised learning, where models learn from labeled data; unsupervised learning, where models find hidden patterns in unlabeled data; and reinforcement learning, where models learn through trial and error. Common algorithms include linear regression, decision trees, neural networks, and support vector machines. Applications range from image recognition and natural language processing to recommendation systems and fraud detection.

Cloud Computing.description: Delivery of computing services over the internet
Cloud Computing.reference: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services including servers, storage, databases, networking, software, analytics, and intelligence over the internet to offer faster innovation, flexible resources, and economies of scale. It eliminates the need for organizations to purchase and maintain physical hardware and software. The main service models are Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS). Deployment models include public cloud, private cloud, and hybrid cloud. Key benefits include cost efficiency, scalability, flexibility, disaster recovery, and automatic updates. Major providers include Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

Artificial Intelligence.description: Simulation of human intelligence in machines
Artificial Intelligence.reference: Artificial Intelligence is the simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems. It involves creating machines that can perform tasks that would typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language understanding. AI encompasses several subfields including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and robotics. AI systems can be categorized as narrow AI, which is designed for specific tasks, and general AI, which can perform any intellectual task a human can. Applications include virtual assistants, autonomous vehicles, medical diagnosis, financial trading, and content recommendation. Ethical considerations include bias, privacy, job displacement, and safety.

Data Science.description: Interdisciplinary field for extracting knowledge from data
Data Science.reference: Data Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms, and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data. It combines elements from statistics, mathematics, computer science, and domain expertise. The data science pipeline involves data collection, data cleaning and preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model building, evaluation, and deployment. Key tools include Python, R, SQL, Hadoop, and Spark. Visualization tools like Tableau and Matplotlib help communicate findings. Data scientists use statistical techniques and machine learning to find patterns, make predictions, and support business decision-making. Applications span healthcare, finance, e-commerce, and social media.

Cyber Security.description: Practice of protecting systems and networks from digital attacks
Cyber Security.reference: Cyber Security is the practice of protecting computer systems, networks, programs, and data from digital attacks, unauthorized access, damage, or theft. It encompasses multiple layers of protection spread across computers, networks, programs, and data. Key areas include network security, application security, information security, operational security, disaster recovery, and end-user education. Common threats include malware, phishing, ransomware, denial of service attacks, man-in-the-middle attacks, and SQL injection. Security frameworks like NIST and ISO 27001 provide guidelines. Technologies used include firewalls, encryption, intrusion detection systems, VPNs, and multi-factor authentication. The CIA triad of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability forms the foundation of cybersecurity principles.

Blockchain.reference: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that maintains a continuously growing list of records called blocks, which are linked and secured using cryptography. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, a timestamp, and transaction data, making it resistant to modification. The blockchain is managed by a peer-to-peer network and validated through consensus mechanisms such as Proof of Work or Proof of Stake. Originally developed for Bitcoin cryptocurrency, blockchain has expanded to smart contracts, supply chain management, healthcare records, and voting systems. Key properties include decentralization, transparency, immutability, and security. Ethereum introduced programmable smart contracts, enabling decentralized applications (dApps) and DeFi platforms.

Internet of Things.description: Network of physical devices connected to the internet
Internet of Things.reference: The Internet of Things refers to the network of physical objects embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity that enables them to collect and exchange data over the internet. IoT devices range from ordinary household items like smart thermostats and refrigerators to sophisticated industrial machinery and city infrastructure. The IoT ecosystem includes devices, connectivity protocols, data processing platforms, and user applications. Communication technologies include WiFi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, Z-Wave, and cellular networks. IoT generates massive amounts of data processed using edge computing and cloud platforms. Applications include smart homes, smart cities, industrial IoT, healthcare monitoring, precision agriculture, and connected vehicles. Security and privacy are major challenges due to the vast number of connected devices.

Operating System.description: Software that manages computer hardware and software resources
Operating System.reference: An Operating System is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs. It acts as an intermediary between users and the computer hardware. Core functions include process management, memory management, file system management, device management, and security. Key concepts include processes and threads, virtual memory and paging, scheduling algorithms like FCFS and Round Robin, file systems like NTFS and ext4, and inter-process communication. Popular operating systems include Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS. The kernel is the core component that manages system resources. Operating systems support multitasking, multiprocessing, and time-sharing to enable multiple programs to run simultaneously.

Database Management System.description: Software for storing, managing, and retrieving structured data
Database Management System.reference: A Database Management System is software that enables users to create, manage, and interact with databases. It provides an organized way to store, retrieve, and manipulate data efficiently. Key concepts include data models such as relational, hierarchical, and NoSQL, SQL language for querying, normalization to reduce redundancy, ACID properties for transaction integrity, indexing for faster retrieval, and concurrency control. Relational databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle use tables with rows and columns. NoSQL databases like MongoDB, Cassandra, and Redis handle unstructured or semi-structured data. Important concepts include ER diagrams, foreign keys, joins, stored procedures, and triggers. Database administrators manage performance, security, backup, and recovery.

Computer Networks.description: Interconnected computing devices that share resources and data
Computer Networks.reference: Computer Networks are systems of interconnected computing devices that can communicate and share resources with each other. Networks are classified by size as LAN, MAN, and WAN, and by topology as bus, star, ring, and mesh. The OSI model defines seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application. The TCP/IP model is the practical implementation used on the internet. Key protocols include IP for addressing, TCP for reliable transmission, UDP for fast transmission, HTTP for web, DNS for domain resolution, and DHCP for automatic IP assignment. Network devices include routers, switches, hubs, and modems. Wireless standards include WiFi (802.11) and cellular networks. Network security involves firewalls, VPNs, and encryption.
